blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.13
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.13

blocks.text: इच्छाशक्तिरुमा कुमारी
blocks.directed: [slowly] इच्छाशक्तिरुमा कुमारी

blocks.text: Icchāśaktir umā kumārī.
blocks.directed: Icchāśaktir umā kumārī.

blocks.text: The power of will is Umā, the Maiden.
blocks.directed: The power of will is Umā, the Maiden.

blocks.text: Śiva’s Girlfriend Turns Out to Be Your Own Will.
blocks.directed: Śiva’s Girlfriend Turns Out to Be Your Own Will.

blocks.text: Here comes Umā.
blocks.directed: Here comes Umā.

blocks.text: Śiva’s consort. The goddess.
blocks.directed: Śiva’s consort. The goddess.

blocks.text: And Vasugupta identifies her with icchāśakti — the power of will.
blocks.directed: And Vasugupta identifies her with icchāśakti — the power of will.

blocks.text: But don’t imagine ordinary personal wanting.
blocks.directed: But don’t imagine ordinary personal wanting.

blocks.text: “I fancy some tea.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I fancy some tea.”

blocks.text: “I want a nicer house.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I want a nicer house.”

blocks.text: “I would quite like that person to reply to my message.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I would quite like that person to reply to my message.”

blocks.text: Those are limited expressions of desire within differentiated existence.
blocks.directed: Those are limited expressions of desire within differentiated existence.

blocks.text: The icchāśakti being described here belongs to the realised yogi whose will is united with the supreme freedom of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The icchāśakti being described here belongs to the realised yogi whose will is united with the supreme freedom of consciousness.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja associates this power with the divine sovereignty of Parabhairava.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja associates this power with the divine sovereignty of Parabhairava.

blocks.text: And the word kumārī, maiden, matters.
blocks.directed: And the word kumārī, maiden, matters.

blocks.text: It points towards the freshness, independence, and unsullied character of this divine power.
blocks.directed: It points towards the freshness, independence, and unsullied character of this divine power.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja offers several interpretive possibilities, including her freedom from limiting associations and her identification with the cosmic play of manifestation and withdrawal. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja offers several interpretive possibilities, including her freedom from limiting associations and her identification with the cosmic play of manifestation and withdrawal. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Consider the three fundamental powers of Śakti:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Consider the three fundamental powers of Śakti:

blocks.text: Icchā — will.
blocks.directed: Icchā — will.

blocks.text: Jñāna — knowledge.
blocks.directed: Jñāna — knowledge.

blocks.text: Kriyā — action.
blocks.directed: Kriyā — action.

blocks.text: In ordinary life, they appear fragmented.
blocks.directed: In ordinary life, they appear fragmented.

blocks.text: You want something.
blocks.directed: You want something.

blocks.text: You don’t know how to obtain it.
blocks.directed: You don’t know how to obtain it.

blocks.text: You try to act.
blocks.directed: You try to act.

blocks.text: You fail.
blocks.directed: You fail.

blocks.text: You become frustrated.
blocks.directed: You become frustrated.

blocks.text: You make tea.
blocks.directed: You make tea.

blocks.text: In the metaphysical description of Śiva, however, will, knowledge and action are powers of the one free consciousness.
blocks.directed: In the metaphysical description of Śiva, however, will, knowledge and action are powers of the one free consciousness.

blocks.text: They are not independent faculties fighting over resources.
blocks.directed: They are not independent faculties fighting over resources.

blocks.text: And the underlying freedom in which these powers belong is precisely what was introduced in the first sūtra.
blocks.directed: And the underlying freedom in which these powers belong is precisely what was introduced in the first sūtra.

blocks.text: Caitanyam ātmā.
blocks.directed: Caitanyam ātmā.

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: Thirteen statements later, we’re discovering what that means for divine agency.
blocks.directed: Thirteen statements later, we’re discovering what that means for divine agency.
